question: Does a replication from the authors' public data reproduce the published difference-in-differences estimates of Card and Krueger (1994), including their standard errors and the regression sample, and how much of the headline estimate remains when extreme store-level employment changes are winsorized, a check for which no published winsorized or trimmed estimate was found (Ropponen's changes-in-changes reanalysis, which studies the distribution of effects, is cited alongside)?
hypotheses: H1 (replication; each target met if |replicated - published| <= 0.05; SE computation fixed at the design gate): (a) Table 3, row 3: NJ-PA difference 2.76 (SE 1.36), with the within-state changes PA -2.16 (1.25) and NJ 0.59 (0.54); (b) Table 3, row 4 (balanced sample): 2.75 (1.34), PA -2.28 (1.25), NJ 0.47 (0.48); (c) Table 4, column (i): 357 stores, New Jersey coefficient 2.33 (SE 1.19). Each part is reported as reproduced or not; the tolerance allows for rounding and for differences between data releases (the public files accompany Myth and Measurement, chapter 2, and may not be identical to the AER files).

H2 (an implementation of Neumark and Wascher's (1995) measurement-error critique; robustness check): on the H1(b) balanced sample, with permanently closed stores set to zero employment in wave 2 and temporarily closed stores missing, winsorize store-level changes in FTE employment at the 5th and 95th percentiles of the pooled distribution of those changes (closures included). H2 holds if the winsorized NJ-minus-PA difference keeps the same sign and at least half the magnitude of the unwinsorized difference on the same sample. Judged on point estimates, not significance (one treated and one control state; Conley and Taber 2011). Secondary, reported but not judged: the same with the six permanently closed stores excluded from winsorization; and Neumark and Wascher's own sample rule (drop closed stores, add chain and ownership controls), for which they report 2.78.
contribution: An independent, fully logged replication of a canonical difference-in-differences estimate from the authors' public data that also targets the published standard errors and the 357-store regression sample, which an earlier informal replication did not reproduce; plus a winsorization check that puts Neumark and Wascher's measurement-error critique into practice; prior distributional reanalyses of these data (e.g. Ropponen's changes-in-changes) are reported in the paper. The crew had read the published results of other robustness checks; what the process rules out is specification search within this study.

tasks.title: The published estimates and definitions; later critiques and robustness checks (e.g. Neumark-Wascher payroll data, Card-Krueger 2000 reply)
